sources.title: The Met: The Sasanian Empire (224 to 651 A.D.), Fowlkes-Childs and Department of Ancient Near Eastern Art
sources.note: Directly read historical summary, 2003 essay revised 2016. Political chronology is independent of the imported 300 to 800 map interval.

sources.title: Betsy Williams, The Sasanians, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2012
sources.note: Directly read sections on scholarship, seventh-century wars and early Islamic continuities.

sources.title: UNESCO: Shushtar Historical Hydraulic System
sources.note: Directly read description and Outstanding Universal Value. Third-century integrated system has earlier roots and many later repairs; the card does not date every surviving component to Sasanian times.

sources.title: St John Simpson, Erk-Kala (ancient Merv): a detailed study of a late Sasanian residence of the 6th to 7th centuries, 2022
sources.note: Original excavation study in Eurasian Steppe Civilization, volume III, 2022. Downloaded institutional PDF and read printed pages 173 to 177, human PDF pages 174 to 178. Floor cleaning and kitchen functions are archaeological interpretations, explicitly described as such.

sources.title: The Met, Bowl with wheel-cut facets, accession 59.34
sources.note: Directly read object record and curatorial description: sixth to seventh century, Iran; manufacturing sequence and distribution of comparable bowls.

sources.title: The Met, Wall frieze with row of leaves, accession 32.150.10
sources.note: Directly read excavated sixth-century Ctesiphon house decoration and repeated molded motifs.

sources.title: British Museum, silver coin of Khusrau II, accession 1920,0515.239
sources.note: Directly read object and inscription catalogue. Exact transliteration hptsyh is translated 37 (regnal year); Pahlavi script is not reconstructed in modern Unicode.

sources.title: Aḥmad Tafażżolī, Education ii: In the Parthian and Sasanian periods, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Directly read scholarly discussion of Pahlavi literary testimony. Most detailed evidence concerns elite and specialist education, not universal school attendance.

sources.title: Lutz Richter-Bernburg, Gondēšāpur ii: History and medical school, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Directly read 2002 article, particularly paragraphs on the circa 610 disputation and first specific hospital mention in 765. Does not support a securely documented Sasanian teaching hospital.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Economy iv: In the Sasanian period
sources.note: Directly read currency discussion: silver drahm around four grams, smaller copper denominations, payments and taxes also in kind.

proposedOverrides.name: Sasanian Empire
proposedOverrides.summary: An Iranian empire connecting western and Central Asia, historically ruled by the dynasty from 224 to 651.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Five coarse century snapshots extend from Mesopotamia through Iran toward Central Asia. The 700 to 800 polygon is incompatible with continued Sasanian rule; public overview and final phase explicitly flag this. No association with separate sasanian-dependencies record.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact museum transliteration hptsyh, translated 37 (regnal year), on circa 626 Khusrau II coin. No invented Pahlavi glyphs.
